notes:
Slope

  • Slope through $(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)$: $m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$. Also $m=\tan\theta$, $\theta$ = inclination.
  • Parallel lines: $m_1=m_2$. Perpendicular lines: $m_1m_2=-1$.

Forms of a line

FormEquation
Point-slope$y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$
Slope-intercept$y=mx+c$
Two-point$y-y_1=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}(x-x_1)$
Intercept$\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{b}=1$
Normal$x\cos\omega+y\sin\omega=p$

General form $Ax+By+C=0$

  • Slope $=-\dfrac{A}{B}$; $x$-intercept $=-\dfrac{C}{A}$; $y$-intercept $=-\dfrac{C}{B}$.

Angle between two lines

  • $\tan\theta = \left|\dfrac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right|$. Lines coincide if $\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}=\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}=\dfrac{C_1}{C_2}$; parallel (distinct) if only the first equality holds.

Distance formulas

  • Point $(x_1,y_1)$ from line $Ax+By+C=0$: $d=\dfrac{|Ax_1+By_1+C|}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}$.
  • Between parallel lines $Ax+By+C_1=0$ and $Ax+By+C_2=0$: $d=\dfrac{|C_1-C_2|}{\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}$.

Family of lines

  • Every line through the intersection of $L_1=0$ and $L_2=0$ can be written as $L_1+\lambda L_2=0$ for some real $\lambda$; find $\lambda$ using any other condition on the required line.

Exam tip

KCET usually asks 2-3 questions from this chapter — slope/equation of a line, distance of a point from a line, distance between parallel lines, and the family-of-lines idea (line through intersection of two given lines) are the most common types. Watch the sign inside the modulus in distance formulas.

questions.q: The equation of the line through $(1,2)$ parallel to $2x+3y=5$ is
questions.explanation: Parallel line has the same slope $-2/3$: $y-2=-\dfrac23(x-1) \Rightarrow 3y-6=-2x+2 \Rightarrow 2x+3y-8=0$.
Slope of first two points $=\dfrac{6-2}{3-1}=2$; slope of last two $=\dfrac{10-6}{5-3}=2$. Equal slopes through a common point mean the three points are collinear.

questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular from the origin to the line $3x+4y=25$ is
questions.explanation: For $ax+by=c$, the foot of the perpendicular from the origin is $\left(\dfrac{ac}{a^2+b^2},\dfrac{bc}{a^2+b^2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{3\times25}{25},\dfrac{4\times25}{25}\right)=(3,4)$.

questions.q: The lines $x+y=1$, $2x+y=2$ and $ax+2y=3$ are concurrent when $a$ equals
questions.explanation: Intersection of the first two: subtracting gives $x=1, y=0$. Substituting into the third line: $a(1)+2(0)=3 \Rightarrow a=3$.

questions.q: The line through the intersection of $x+y-2=0$ and $2x-y+1=0$, parallel to $y=x$, is
questions.explanation: Family: $(x+y-2)+\lambda(2x-y+1)=0$. Matching slope 1 (parallel to $y=x$) gives $\lambda=-2$, and the equation simplifies to $3x-3y+4=0$.

For every value of $\lambda$, the line $(x+y-3)+\lambda(2x-y)=0$ passes through the fixed point
questions.explanation: The line passes through the point common to $x+y-3=0$ and $2x-y=0$ for every $\lambda$. Solving these: $y=2x$ and $x+2x=3 \Rightarrow x=1, y=2$.
